title: New compulsory third-party (green slip) scheme (New South Wales)
summary: A new CTP scheme commenced on 1 December 2017, moving NSW to defined benefits for most injuries with insurer profit normalisation and risk equalisation; private insurers already competed before.
direction_rationale: Insurers already competed; the reform mainly cut claims costs and premiums. Profit normalisation and risk equalisation narrow the room for insurers to compete on price, so the competition effect is unclear.
comparison: Victoria and Tasmania keep public monopoly insurers (TAC, MAIB); Queensland has private insurers with regulated premiums
confounders: benefit changes lower claims costs whatever competition does

assessment.summary: A new compulsory third-party scheme with defined benefits for most injuries, insurer profit normalisation and risk equalisation. Claims costs and premiums fell, but limits on profits and risk pricing narrow how insurers compete.

marks.reason: Defined benefits reduce the legal and claims-handling costs of fault-based disputes.
Profit normalisation and risk equalisation narrow the room for insurers to compete on price.
